questions.question: GAO's 2026 assessment shows a percentage decrease in the CVN 78 program's unit cost. Does this mean CVN 79 has become less expensive?
questions.reference_answer: No. The Navy added two ships, and the unit cost is averaged across all six ships. As a result, the unit cost decreased even though costs for the three ships already in development increased. CVN 79's costs have increased by over $1.5 billion since 2021.

questions.question: GAO-15-22 cites an $11.5 billion cost cap for CVN 79, GAO-17-575 cites $11.4 billion, and CRS cites $11,398.0 million. Do these represent three different cost caps?
questions.source: gao-15-22Cost Cap Legislation.pdf PDF p.11; gao-17-575 PDF p.6; RS20643.302 CRS PDF p.11
questions.reference_answer: No. There are two caps, not three. The $11.5 billion cap is the earlier cap, raised in 2013 and established for follow-on ships by the FY2014 NDAA. Section 122 of the FY2016 NDAA established the $11,398.0 million cap, which GAO-17-575 rounds to $11.4 billion.

questions.question: CRS reports $13,196.0 million as CVN-79's total procurement cost, while the PB 2027 SCN P-5c reports a Total Ship Estimate of $13,409.970 million. Which figure should be used as the current estimate for reconciliation, and why?
questions.source: RS20643.302 CRS PDF p.8; SCN_Book PB27.pdf PDF p.95
questions.reference_answer: The PB 2027 P-5c figure ($13,409.970 million), because CRS cites the FY2026 budget submission, whereas PB 2027 is the later budget.

questions.question: FPDS-NG and USAspending show a $583,963.00 difference for the CVN 79 construction preparation contract. Should this variance be investigated as a reconciliation error?
questions.source: aircarrier_variances E-16 (project register, not a public document)
questions.reference_answer: No. This is an as-of-date difference because the two systems were accessed on different dates. The variance is recorded as resolved (E-16).

questions.reference_answer: It did not increase the cap. The FY2020 NDAA's revised caps retained the CVN-79 cap at $11,398.0 million, the same amount established by the FY2016 NDAA and retained by the FY2018 NDAA.
